question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer, CIO of Aravalli Long-Only Fund (Category III AIF), is briefing the board on the fund's strategy. Which statement BEST describes the Long-only Equity Strategy as per the SEBI chapter framework?

answer.text: The manager takes only long positions in selected stocks using top-down or bottom-up fundamental analysis; Put options or index short futures may be used purely to hedge market risk.
The manager takes 130% long and 30% short across the portfolio to maintain 100% net exposure.
The manager keeps portfolio Beta at exactly zero by equal rupee long and short positions.
The manager switches between net long and net short bias based on macro signals across asset classes.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 10.1.1.1, a Long-only Strategy focuses on absolute return with capital preservation using only long positions; hedges (index Put options, short index futures) may be added ONLY to reduce market risk, not to create short exposure. The Trap: Option B describes 130/30 Long-short; Option C describes Market-neutral; Option D describes Global-macro/Directional. All are real Cat III strategies but distinct from Long-only. Note: Long-only Cat III is distinct from Long-short (130/30), Market-neutral (zero-beta), and Directional/Global-macro strategies even though all are permitted Cat III approaches. Hedging instruments (Put options, short index futures) can be used only to reduce market risk on the long book.
